head_commit.message:
Add automated coverage pipeline from MongoDB jstest fingerprints

Builds a pipeline that mines MongoDB's jstests for query patterns and
generates catalog entries covering all 3384 fingerprinted queries (up
from 702). Coverage files are generated into automation/coverage/ and
loaded by catalog/query/coverage/ scaffolds at runtime.

Key changes:
- compiler.ts: make Struct recursive (was artificially capped at 1
  level due to a TypeScript circular type alias limitation)
- fingerprint.ts: expose the fingerprinter store so generate-coverage
  can read slot assignments after co-fingerprinting docs and queries
- generate-coverage.ts: groups gap records by document structure,
  assigns stable field names and nudged values per group, reconstructs
  queries and documents, generates type/operator variants
- scaffold-coverage.ts: generates catalog .ts files that load from
  the companion JSON; skip-if-exists to preserve manual edits

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: derive BSON stub randomness from a per-file seed

Random.rand(), ISODate(), and ObjectId() previously fell back to
Math.random()/wall-clock time when unseeded, so re-extracting an
unchanged jstest produced different output every run (Random.setRandomSeed()
was also a silent no-op). That churn cascaded into unrelated diffs in
mongo-catalog's coverage files on every scheduled update.

Seed a mulberry32 PRNG per file (via an FNV-1a hash of the file path)
so extraction is reproducible across runs while still varying between
files and call sites.

head_commit.message:
feat: migrate test runner to node:test, rewrite $near/$nearSphere, add catalog-overrides mechanism

Test infrastructure:
- Rewire npm test/test:full onto scripts/test.ts's node:test runner,
  filtered by operators.json's working status, abandoning the legacy
  tape runner as the default
- Add source/Test/catalog-overrides.json + Catalog.spec.ts support for
  todo/expect overrides, so known ground-truth divergences (deliberate
  scope exclusions, upstream library bugs, unexplained mysteries) are
  checked in as honest, verifiable facts instead of silently invisible
  or permanently failing
- Migrate legacy tape tests for Geospatial to source/**/*.spec.ts

BSON/rendering:
- Add render() to Domain/BSON.ts's classifiers dispatch, reproducing
  MongoDB's own BSON debug-print format (Date, RegExp, arrays, nested
  values) for error messages that echo back the offending value
- Fix two dispatch bugs found while merging render() in (raw .find()
  instead of detect(), and an array-map index-corruption bug)

$near/$nearSphere:
- Rewrite $geometry argument parsing entirely (NearGeometry.ts) to
  match MongoDB's actual multi-branch behavior, byte-for-byte on error
  text against ground truth
- Add LineString/Polygon nearest-point support for both the GeoJSON
  and (now) legacy coordinate forms
- Root-cause and improve the legacy $nearSphere antimeridian guard:
  replaced a wrong raw-longitude-difference check with a flat/Euclidean
  secondary gate alongside the real haversine bound; one residual case
  (geoAntipodal doc 7) is confirmed mathematically irreducible

Geospatial fixes:
- $box with 3+ corners was silently becoming a polygon instead of a
  rectangle (legacyToGeoJSON's ambiguous dispatch checks isLegacyPolygon
  first); added legacyBoxToGeoJSON() so $box's own compiler no longer
  goes through shape-guessing at all
- $box/$polygon/$center/$geoIntersects now correctly match both legacy-
  and GeoJSON-shaped document fields (previously legacy-only or
  GeoJSON-only depending on the operator)
- Added crs validation ($geoWithin), matching MongoDB's two distinct
  error messages for a non-object crs vs. an unrecognized name
- Compiler.ts: fixed an always-true sibling-key filter condition; added
  SiblingKey.ts as the generalized claimed-key mechanism

Remaining known gaps are tracked precisely in catalog-overrides.json
and plans/geospatial-completeness.md (workspace root) — 9/458 geo
operations still mismatch ground truth, all parked deliberately with
accurate reasons, not silently dropped.

head_commit.message:
fix: don't count a lone boundary touch as a LineString intersecting a Polygon

A line whose only contact with a polygon was one point on its boundary
(commonly a shared vertex) counted as intersecting even when the rest
of the line stayed entirely outside. Checked per segment now: a strict
transversal crossing or a genuinely interior endpoint proves real
extent; a bare touch, without either, no longer does. Collinear overlap
(#30) is unchanged. Independent of the boundary option — this is about
whether the line has any actual extent, not which points count as "on"
the polygon.

Closes #31

head_commit.message:
fix: detect collinear, overlapping LineStrings as intersecting

isLinesCrossing's parametric formula assumes exactly one intersection
point, which isn't true for two segments lying on the same line — they
can share a whole overlapping stretch, or none. Falls back to checking
whether any endpoint of one line lies on the other whenever the lines
are parallel (including the degenerate zero-length case), using a
looser tolerance than isPointOnLine's default since two independently-
computed collinear points land ~1e-9–1e-10 m apart, not bit-exact.

Closes #30

fix: stop treating a ring with one duplicate vertex as fully degenerate

#27's guard only caught a ring collapsed to a single point. A ring

closing wrap) are now collapsed before the ring math runs.

(isInclusiveEdge, winding, isPointInRing) — no behavior change there.

fix: stop treating every point as inside a degenerate (coincident-vertex) ring

A ring whose vertices all collapse to the same point (e.g. a legacy
$box query with equal corners) matched every point tested against it.
isPositionInSphericalRing's crossing-count parity can't register a

point; getClosestPointOnLineByPoint independently divided by zero on
the same zero-length edge, masked until the first bug was fixed. Only
the coincident point itself is inside now, matching real MongoDB.

feat: add 'winding' boundary convention, the top-left fill rule for lon/lat

A boundary point is included if its edge heads south, or heads east
along a line of constant latitude; a shared vertex requires both
incident edges to agree, so a boundary is claimed by exactly one
ring instead of being double-counted or left with a gap. Reversing
a ring's winding flips every boundary answer, unlike 'include'/
'exclude'.

Closes #25

head_commit.message:
fix: don't count a lone boundary touch as a LineString intersecting a Polygon

A line whose only contact with a polygon was one point on its boundary
(commonly a shared vertex) counted as intersecting even when the rest
of the line stayed entirely outside. Checked per segment now: a strict
transversal crossing or a genuinely interior endpoint proves real
extent; a bare touch, without either, no longer does. Collinear overlap
(#30) is unchanged. Independent of the boundary option — this is about
whether the line has any actual extent, not which points count as "on"
the polygon.

Closes #31

head_commit.message:
fix: detect collinear, overlapping LineStrings as intersecting

isLinesCrossing's parametric formula assumes exactly one intersection
point, which isn't true for two segments lying on the same line — they
can share a whole overlapping stretch, or none. Falls back to checking
whether any endpoint of one line lies on the other whenever the lines
are parallel (including the degenerate zero-length case), using a
looser tolerance than isPointOnLine's default since two independently-
computed collinear points land ~1e-9–1e-10 m apart, not bit-exact.

Closes #30

head_commit.message:
fix: stop treating a ring with one duplicate vertex as fully degenerate

#27's guard only caught a ring collapsed to a single point. A ring
with 3+ distinct vertices but one listed twice in a row still has a
zero-length edge that crossing-count parity can't see, so it kept
misreporting rings that were only partially degenerate. Vertices
adjacent to a zero-length edge (including across the ring's own
closing wrap) are now collapsed before the ring math runs.

Also restores a few explanatory comments lost from earlier commits
(isInclusiveEdge, winding, isPointInRing) — no behavior change there.

Closes #29

head_commit.message:
fix: stop treating every point as inside a degenerate (coincident-vertex) ring

A ring whose vertices all collapse to the same point (e.g. a legacy
$box query with equal corners) matched every point tested against it.
isPositionInSphericalRing's crossing-count parity can't register a
crossing against a zero-length edge, so it trivially agreed for any
point; getClosestPointOnLineByPoint independently divided by zero on
the same zero-length edge, masked until the first bug was fixed. Only
the coincident point itself is inside now, matching real MongoDB.

Closes #27

head_commit.message:
feat: add 'winding' boundary convention, the top-left fill rule for lon/lat

A boundary point is included if its edge heads south, or heads east
along a line of constant latitude; a shared vertex requires both
incident edges to agree, so a boundary is claimed by exactly one
ring instead of being double-counted or left with a gap. Reversing
a ring's winding flips every boundary answer, unlike 'include'/
'exclude'.

Closes #25

6378100 m $nearSphere radius) or get raw angular/planar values (radius

the formulas outside the library. Requested by Monger; distance() is left
untouched since it doesn't need the radius plumbing.
